title: Check a small engine's oil with the dipstick: pull, wipe, reseat, pull again to read, and reseat it
instruction: Check the oil level on the engine with the dipstick, then put everything back.
context: Small engine mechanics, outdoor power equipment technicians and quick-lube technicians check the oil on mowers, generators and pumps many times a day (O*NET 49-3053.00, Outdoor Power Equipment and Other Small Engine Mechanics). The job is to read the oil level on the dipstick and leave the engine closed up, and the rule is that the first pull is never read: oil splashed up the fill tube coats the blade above the true level, so the dipstick is pulled, wiped clean on a rag, pushed back in until the cap seats fully (a part-way push reads low or smears again), pulled a second time and held still, tip down, to read the crosshatch, then pushed back in until it seats so dirt cannot get into the crankcase, and the rag is put down. A first-pull reading hides a low level, and running low on oil is the most common way small engines are ruined.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. A bench model of a small four-stroke engine, as on a lawn mower or portable generator, is fixed on the table: a wooden mounting board (x 22 to 38, y -22 to -7, 0.8 cm thick), an aluminum crankcase and cylinder block (x 27 to 37, y -21 to -9, up to z 7) under a red flywheel shroud (to z 10), and a fill boss on the crankcase's front. A yellow oil fill tube, 2.4 cm across, rises from the boss to its mouth at z 8.5, on an axis at x 25, y -12. The dipstick sits seated in the tube: a steel blade 1.0 x 0.3 x 8 cm with a crosshatch between its ADD and FULL marks 0.8 to 2.0 cm from the tip, a yellow cap disc 3.2 cm across and 1 cm tall resting on the tube's rim, and a yellow T-handle 3.5 cm wide (along y), 1.8 cm thick and 3.5 cm tall on top; 12.5 cm overall, 40 g. It slides only along the tube's axis and falls back down the tube if let go. The blade's lower 6 cm carries a dark smear of oil (drawn), the false first reading. A folded blue shop rag, a pad 4 x 4 x 2.5 cm of 40 g, lies loose on the table centered at x 26, y 10. Both arms start at their home poses.
scoring: q = the dipstick cap's height above its seat. Out = q at least the blade length plus 5 mm (tip clear of the mouth); seated = q of 3 mm or less (a 3 mm lift of the cap is visible). Held = a tool point within 3 cm of the handle's middle with its fingers closed. Wipe: while the blade is out and smeared, the rag touches it when its middle is within 2.7 cm of the blade's axis (half the pad, the blade's half-thickness and 0.5 cm of cloth pressed round it), its outline is within 2 mm of the blade's faces (a rigid pad held clear does not count), and its height overlaps the blade above the mouth; the blade is wiped once the rag's middle, sliding while touching (only between two touching steps, at most 5 mm per step, so dabs and jumps add nothing), has slid over 80% (3.2 cm) of the blade's lower 4 cm in that pull. The pad reaches 2 cm either side of its middle, so that stroke drags cloth over the whole 6 cm smear and the marks, and 80% leaves 8 mm of slack for the arm's lag. A dab or half a stroke is not a wipe; two strokes in one pull add up; the tip going back into the tube clears the count; either hand may move. Reseat = the wiped blade pushed in by hand until seated; a part-way push that comes out again smears it again; a drop or a seat without a wipe restarts the procedure. Reading = after the reseat, pulled out again and held out and still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. Scores: 0 if never wiped and pushed back in until the cap seats (doing nothing, a first-pull reading, skipping the wipe, a dab or half-length wipe, a half-seated reinsert, or a stick dropped back in); 0.25 wiped and seated but no true reading (the second pull not held out still for 1 s); 0.5 true reading but then left out, part way in, dropped back or still held; 0.75 dipstick seated by hand and let go (tool points over 6 cm from the handle) but the rag not put down (at rest, within 1 cm of the table, tool points over 6 cm from it); 1.0 all of it with both arms home and still for 1 s, else 0.9. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1.0. A real trial is checked from the video: count the pulls, check the rag is drawn along at least 3.2 cm of the lower blade between them, check the gap under the cap after each push with a 3 mm feeler strip, time the second pull's hold, and check the rag is back on the table.
reset_notes: Seat the dipstick, smear oil on its blade's lower 6 cm (and up the inside of the tube for a real trial), and put the rag back at x 26, y 10. The oil level in a real engine stays between ADD and FULL.
fidelity: The dipstick is real size for a mower or generator engine; a longer one could not be pulled clear by arms that lift about 22 cm. It stays on the tube's axis even when out (a guide), so it is read tip down and falls back down the tube if let go. The oil film, its removal by the rag and the true level are drawn from the scorer's state, not simulated, and the rag is a rigid pad.
